vMatrix.notes: How the trio and mandatory-node memberships were verified: the class doc conveys all of them as bare skill-icon images with no text captions, which is exactly the failure mode that produced the original defect in this file. Every icon in the 'Mandatory Boost Nodes' row, the '2 Node Setup' block and the '1 Node Setup' block was downloaded and MD5-matched, byte for byte, against the icons in the same document's own labelled per-skill reference tables. All 18 matched exactly, so these memberships are decoded, not inferred. The class doc and the independent trio table agree on BOTH trios of the 2-node setup, which is stronger than this file previously recorded. Grandis Library's Primary/Secondary/Other tiering for Shadower (Node 1 Assassinate; Node 2 Meso Explosion; Node 3 Dark Flare + Cruel Stab; Node 4 Sudden Raid + Shadow Veil; Node 5 Phase Dash; Node 6 Midnight Carnival + Savage Blow) is credited in its own credits block to the class doc, so it is a dependent restatement and is not counted as a second opinion. No source reachable in this pass gives a numeric node-leveling roadmap (which node to take to 25/30/40/50/60 in what order), so levelingRoadmap is null. The V Matrix does not exist below Lv 200, so this section is forward-planning only for a Lv 140 character.

gearingNotes: Crit rate is unusually cheap for this class. The class doc says Shadower assembles most of it from its own kit - roughly 50% between Flip of the Coin and Critical Edge, plus base crit - and then tops up to 100% with Decent Sharp Eyes, the Beast Tamer link, Night Lord and Marksman Legion ranks and Legion/hyper stat points, leaving roughly 15% to buy. The practical consequence is that once 100% is reached, hyper stat and inner ability points other classes spend on crit rate are free to go elsewhere. Ignore Enemy Defense: Shadower Instinct supplies a 20% IED buff, and the class doc gives visual-IED targets of roughly 96-97% for 380 PDR bosses, 93-95% for Black Mage and Chaos Tenebris, and 91%+ for earlier bosses. Meso: the class doc states Shadower carries a 20% additive Meso Obtained effect that other classes do not have, which is why Meso Obtained lines are recommended on Reboot/Heroic. Attack speed: the doc's stack is base 6, Booster +2, green potion +1, Decent Speed Infusion +1, and it takes the position that reaching 0 attack speed is not required. Secondary weapon: the doc names Deimos Shield as BIS - note Shadower can equip a shield rather than a throwing-star-class secondary, which is a real gearing difference from Night Lord. Potential: the doc recommends at least two lines of 8% critical damage on gloves. All of the above is single-sourced to the class doc; none of it was confirmed by a second independent page in this pass. NAME CORRECTION 2026-09-12: this field previously read 'Flip the Coin'. The in-game name is 'Flip of the Coin' per MapleStory Wiki (Hyper Skill, Active, Lv. 140, Critical Rate +25%, Damage +24%), and the class doc's own skill table spells it 'Flip of the coin'. The wrong spelling appears to have come from the 2022 DigitalTQ page, which writes 'Flip The Coin'.

commonMistakes.mistake: Building a HEXA mastery core before its underlying boost node is at Lv. 40. The class doc states this gate verbatim for three of the four mastery cores: Core 2 requires Meso Explosion at V Matrix Lv. 40+, Core 3 requires Dark Flare and Cruel Stab at Lv. 40+, Core 4 requires Sudden Raid and Shadow Veil at Lv. 40+ (all 'before Matrix Points'). It states no such gate for Core 1.
Chasing 0 attack speed. The class doc says it is not necessary for Shadower.

Content outside the five endgame sections - jobs 1-4 skill points, damage coefficients, rotations, job tiers - was out of scope for this pass and was neither re-verified nor changed.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm.
contest.resolutionMethod: Every disputed endgame claim was re-checked against the exact page already cited. The class doc was fetched as raw HTML and read verbatim. Because its build diagrams are images with no text, each icon in the Mandatory Boost Nodes row, the 2 Node Setup block, the 1 Node Setup block and the Node Priority row was downloaded and MD5-matched byte-for-byte against the icons in the same document's own labelled per-skill reference tables, giving a deterministic decode rather than a visual guess. MapleStory Wiki was read through a browser session (it 403s plain fetches). The independent trio table, MapleDoro, Grandis Library and DigitalTQ were each re-fetched.

resolved.defect: Bossing-mule trio third member: the file states the 1-node setup is Assassinate / Meso Explosion / Dark Flare. The class doc's actual text names Cruel Stab ('You can use cruel stab node to help level'), not Dark Flare. Trio memberships in the doc are image icons with no text enumeration, so Dark Flare was reconstructed. Recorded conflict #1 is built on this incorrect reading.
resolved.what: Both the file and the critic were half right. Byte-matching the icons shows the class doc's 'Example: 1 Node Setup' block contains TWO icon rows, not one: Assassinate / Meso Explosion / Dark Flare and Assassinate / Meso Explosion / Cruel Stab. Dark Flare is genuinely shown, and the Cruel Stab variant the critic pointed at was genuinely missing. The trio entry now records both variants, and the prose sentence about Cruel Stab is quoted as the explanation for the second one.

resolved.defect: The entire seven-step hexa.order sequence as a sourced priority order. The class doc conveys its 'Sixth Job Upgrade Order' only as an embedded image; no text list states any ordering. The published sequence is identical to MapleStory Wiki's game-data slot numbering, which is the expected signature of an order reconstructed from a data table and then attributed to a guide's judgement.
resolved.what: Defect upheld in full. The doc's 'Sixth Job Upgrade Order' heading is followed immediately by its 'Hexa Stat' heading with one image between them and zero words of text; the image is a grid of roughly 150 icon cells each stamped with a target level - a granular roadmap, not the coarse seven-step core ordering the file published. The icons in that grid could not be resolved, so nothing can be published from it. hexa.order has been deleted and replaced by hexa.cores, an UNORDERED inventory flagged ordered:false, carrying only what is actually verifiable: each core's game-data slot membership (MapleStory Wiki, cross-checked against the class doc's own 6th job skill tables) and the three Lv. 40 boost-node unlock gates quoted verbatim from the class doc.

resolved.defect: 'Flip the Coin' in gearingNotes - the actual skill name on MapleStory Wiki is 'Flip of the Coin' (Hyper Skill, Active, Level Requirement 140, Critical Rate +25%, Damage +24%).
resolved.scope: gearingNotes - strictly outside the five endgame sections, but a cheap verified factual name error, so corrected rather than left
resolved.what: Confirmed against MapleStory Wiki (Flip of the Coin, Lv. 140, Critical Rate +25%, Damage +24%) and against the class doc's own skill table, which spells it 'Flip of the coin'. gearingNotes now reads 'Flip of the Coin' with a note recording the correction. The wrong spelling traces to the 2022 DigitalTQ page, which writes 'Flip The Coin'.

resolved.defect: OMISSION rather than invention, but equally material: Decent Holy Symbol is named a mandatory boost node by the class doc and appears nowhere in the file. This also falsifies the file's claim that 'the doc gives no second full trio for a main' - the doc has a 2-node setup with two trios.
resolved.what: Both halves upheld, with one precision fix. Decent Holy Symbol is now recorded, under vMatrix.specialNodes rather than under boost nodes, because it is a 5th job common skill node and not a boost node - the class doc discusses it inside its V-Matrix section and ranks it 5th in its own Node Priority row. Its recommendation is quoted verbatim. Separately, the false claim that the doc gives no second full trio for a main has been removed: the doc's recommended 2-node setup has two trios, Assassinate / Meso Explosion / Shadow Veil and Sudden Raid / Dark Flare / Cruel Stab, and those are the same two sets the independent trio table gives.

resolved.defect: NOT RAISED BY THE CRITIC - found during resolution. hyperSkills.passives claimed 'moderate' consensus on the strength of DigitalTQ as a second independent source for the five mandatory passive picks.
resolved.what: Re-reading DigitalTQ shows it does not list those five picks: under its hyper skill heading it names Flip The Coin, Shadow Veil and Epic Adventure, which are the three ACTIVES, and describes the passives only loosely. The citation was an inversion. DigitalTQ has been dropped as a source for the passives, and all five picks are now labelled sourceCount 1 / consensus weak. Grandis lists the same five but credits the class doc.

resolved.defect: NOT RAISED BY THE CRITIC - found during resolution. hyperStats shipped two ORDERED arrays labelled 'priority'.
resolved.what: The class doc prints the stats as an unnumbered stacked list and never calls it a ranking; in the same section it says to split points evenly and to use a calculator. Array order was therefore asserting a claim the source does not make. hyperStats is now ordered:false with the stats as unordered sets, the document's literal print sequence preserved in a separate clearly-labelled field, and the doc's three hedging sentences quoted verbatim under caveats.

resolved.defect: NOT RAISED BY THE CRITIC - found during resolution. hyperSkills.passives.situational merged two distinct hyper passives into one entry, 'Cruel Stab - Spread: Max Enemies Hit +2; Number of Attacks +1'.
resolved.what: The class doc prints two consecutive rows both labelled 'Cruel Stab - Spread', one with each effect. Per MapleStory Wiki these are two different skills: Cruel Stab - Spread (Lv. 165, Max Enemies Hit +2) and Cruel Stab - Extra Strike (Lv. 180, Number of Attacks +1). The class doc's label on the second is wrong. Both are now separate entries under their in-game names.

resolved.defect: NOT RAISED BY THE CRITIC - found during resolution. vMatrix.priority said of Sudden Raid that 'The class doc explicitly ranks it below the mandatory group.'
resolved.what: Citation inversion. Sudden Raid IS inside the class doc's mandatory boost node icon row and is described under the 'Mandatory Boost Nodes' heading. What the doc actually says is that it 'doesn't really add much damage to the kit' - a lukewarm description inside the mandatory set, not a demotion out of it. The entry now states that it is in the mandatory set and quotes the deprioritising sentence as such.

resolved.defect: NOT RAISED BY THE CRITIC - found during resolution. innerAbility was split into bossing / training / earlyGame blocks with line ranks that do not match the source.
resolved.what: The class doc does not split inner ability by bossing versus training. It gives one Ideal Inner Ability Lines table with a Legendary column and a Unique column, two unlabelled example BIS setups in a two-column table, and prose caveats. Two rank errors fixed: Item Drop Rate 15-20% is a LEGENDARY line, not Unique; Damage to monsters with Abnormal Status 7-8% is a UNIQUE line, not 'Unique/Epic'. The invented bossing/training labels on the two BIS setups were removed, as was an added clause about when to replace the early-game crit rate line that the doc does not contain.

resolved.defect: NOT RAISED BY THE CRITIC - found during resolution. hyperSkills.actives was null with the note that actives 'could not be sourced from a current page'.
resolved.what: There is nothing to source, because there is no decision to make: MapleStory Wiki lists exactly three active hyper skills for Shadower, at Lv. 140, 160 and 190, one per active hyper point. The field now lists Flip of the Coin, Shadow Veil and Epic Adventure with selectionRequired:false and an explicit note that this is game data rather than a recommendation.

resolved.defect: NOT RAISED BY THE CRITIC - found during resolution. The class doc's ordered 'Node Priority' row (Highest to Lowest) was never captured at all, because it is an image.
resolved.what: The row's 22 icons were decoded by byte-matching and are now published as vMatrix.nodeTypePriority with ordered:true - this is the one genuinely ordered V-matrix claim any source makes for Shadower. Three icons matched nothing labelled in the document and are recorded as UNIDENTIFIED placeholders rather than guessed.
